The main takeaway from our work is that
the Unkar Group records the tectonic history of southwestern Laurentia at a time when the Grenville orogen was still active.

there was a prolonged period of Grenville-age orogeny that was not limited to the Grenville province, but was also active in southwestern Laurentia, and that this period was punctuated by two phases of deformation, the earlier of which was characterized by NW shortening, and the latter by NE-SW extension.

Grenville-age orogenic processes extended into the Mesoproterozoicoic and persisted for at least 150 million years, with implications for the timing of the Grenville orogeny and the tectonic setting of the Mesoproterozic Unkar Group and Grand Canyon Supergoup in general.
